The purchaser also reserves the right to increase the ordered quantity up to 25% of the contracted quantity during the currency of the contract at the contracted rates. The delivery period of quantity shall commence from the last date of original delivery order and in cases where option clause is exercised during the extended delivery period the additional time shall commence from the last date of extended delivery period. The additional delivery time shall be (Increased quantity ÷ Original quantity) × Original delivery period (in days), subject to minimum of 30 days. If the original delivery period is less than 30 days, the additional time equals the original delivery period. The Purchaser may extend this calculated delivery duration up to the original delivery period while exercising the option clause. Bidders must comply with these terms. 2. Scope of Supply Scope of supply (Bid price to include all cost components) : Supply Installation Testing and Commissioning of Goods 3. Service & Support Dedicated /toll Free Telephone No. for Service Support : BIDDER/OEM must have Dedicated/toll Free Telephone No. for Service Support. 4. Certificates Material Test Certificate Should Be Sent Along with The Supply. The Material Will Be Checked by Buyer’s Lab & the Results of the Lab will be the Sole Criteria for Acceptance of the Item. 5. Warranty Warranty period of the supplied products shall be 3 years from the date of final acceptance of goods or after completion of installation, commissioning & testing of goods (if included in the scope of supply), at consignee location. OEM Warranty certificates must be submitted by Successful Bidder at the time of delivery of Goods. The seller should guarantee the rectification of goods in case of any break down during the guarantee period. Seller should have well established Installation, Commissioning, Training, Troubleshooting and Maintenance Service group in INDIA for attending the after sales service. Details of Service Centres near consignee destinations are to be uploaded along with the bid. 6. Warranty Bidder / OEM has to give an undertaking that after expiry of warranty period, it will provide AMC Service for next 2 years for the offered products at the rate not more than 5 % of contract price per annum. Buyer reserves the right to enter into an AMC agreement ( covering preventive maintenance and servicing)with the Successful Bidder / OEM after expiry of the Warranty period at rate as mentioned above and the payment for the AMC charges would be made Annually after rendering of the AMC Services of the relevant AMC period. Performance Security of the successful bidder shall be forfeited if it fails to accept the AMC contract when called upon by the buyer. The original Performance Security of contract will be returned only after submission and verification of AMC Performance Security for 2% of total AMC value valid up to AMC period plus 2 months (if there is no other claim). (Undertaking of acceptance to be uploaded with bid).

7. Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses Mandatory Pre-Bid Meeting and Product Sample Demonstration Attendance at the Pre-Bid Meeting shall be mandatory for all participating bidders. Further, bidders shall be required to physically demonstrate and submit/display the sample of the of fered product for inspection and verification by the competent authority, as specified in the tender. Failure to attend the Pre-Bid Meeting and/or failure to demonstrate the product sam ple shall result in disqualification of the bidder, and the bid shall be rejected as non-respons ive. Most importantly, the bidder shall have to see the ground situation and calculate/ adju st his bidding content and quoted price accordingly. Hence pre bid interaction is a mandato ry requirement. WARRANTY, DEFECT LIABILITY AND ANNUAL MAINTENANCE CONTRACT (AMC) 1. Warranty Period. 1.1 All items, equipment, materials, components, structures and installations for ming part of the Battle Obstacle Course shall carry a minimum comprehensive warra nty of three (03) years commencing from the date of successful completion of install ation, commissioning, inspection and formal acceptance of the entire work by the co mpetent authority. 1.2 During the warranty period, the Contractor shall, at no additional cost to the Department, rectify all defects, deficiencies and failures arising from defective mater ials, poor workmanship, faulty fabrication, improper installation, structural inadequa cy or premature deterioration. This shall include repair, restoration or replacement o f defective components, as applicable. 1.3 All expenditure towards labour, materials, transportation, tools, equipment, dismantling, reinstallation and other incidental activities required for rectification of defects during the warranty period shall be borne entirely by the Contractor. No addi tional payment shall be admissible on this account. 2. Annual Maintenance Contract (AMC). 2.1 In addition to the above warranty, the Contractor shall provide a comprehens ive Annual Maintenance Contract (AMC) for a further period of two (02) years, comm encing immediately upon expiry of the three-year warranty period. Accordingly, the Contractor's warranty and maintenance obligations shall extend for a total period of five (05) years from the date of formal acceptance of the completed work. 2.2 The AMC shall include periodic inspection, preventive maintenance, servicin g, repair, restoration and replacement of defective, damaged or worn-out componen ts to ensure that all obstacles remain safe, structurally sound, serviceable and opera tional throughout the AMC period. 2.3 The cost of the AMC, including manpower, labour, supervision, tools, equipm ent, transportation, materials and replacement of all components covered under the AMC, shall be deemed included in the quoted contract price. No additional financial l iability shall be admissible to the Department for such services. 3. Items Specifically Excluded from AMC. 3.1 The following items, being consumable or expendable in nature, shall be excl uded from the scope of AMC: 3.1.1. Plastic ropes used in the Robber's Climb obstacle.

3.1.2 Sand used for cushioning, impact absorption and safety surfacing in in dividual obstacles. 3.2 Replenishment or replacement of the above excluded items, when required due to normal usage, depletion or consumption, shall be undertaken on payment at the prevailing market rates applicable at the time of replacement, subject to prior as sessment and written approval of the Department. 3.3 The Contractor shall submit the requirement, quantity and applicable rate for approval before undertaking any such replacement. No unilateral expenditure or sub sequent financial claim shall be entertained by the Department. 3.4 The above exclusions shall not absolve the Contractor of responsibility for an y premature damage, failure or deterioration of associated structural arrangements attributable to defective materials, poor workmanship or improper installation. 4. Items Specifically Included under AMC. 4.1 Notwithstanding their susceptibility to wear and tear arising from normal usa ge and exposure to weather conditions, the following items and associated maintena nce activities shall be expressly covered under the AMC and shall not be treated as c onsumable or expendable items:- 4.1.1. Manila ropes. 4.1.2. Jute mats. 4.1.3. Nuts, bolts, fasteners and associated fixing arrangements. 4.1.4. Painting, repainting, surface treatment and anti-corrosion protection of structural components. 4.1.5 Barbed wire. 4.1.6. Pickets. 4.1.7 Welding, repair and reinforcement of iron/steel components forming part of t he obstacles. 4.1.8 Wooden planks, ballies and other wooden structural components forming par t of the obstacles. 4.2 The Contractor shall undertake necessary inspection, tightening, repair, reco nditioning, replacement or renewal of the above items, wherever required, without a ny additional financial liability to the Department. 4.3 Replacement of any of the above components shall be with materials of equi valent or superior quality conforming to the original technical specifications and app roved by the Department. 5. Response Time and Rectification Timelines. 5.1 The Contractor shall nominate a responsible representative and provide cont act details for lodging maintenance complaints throughout the warranty and AMC pe riods. 5.2 Upon receipt of a complaint or maintenance requirement from the Department, t he Contractor shall: 5.2.1. Acknowledge the complaint within 24 hours. 5.2.2. Depute a representative and undertake inspection within 48 hours. 5.2.3. Complete rectification of defects and restoration of the affected obsta cle within seven (07) calendar days from receipt of the complaint. 5.3 In cases involving structural defects, safety hazards or any condition renderi ng an obstacle unsafe for use, the Contractor shall immediately respond and initiate

necessary corrective measures. The affected obstacle shall remain out of use until c ertified safe by the competent authority. 5.4 Where rectification within the stipulated period is not feasible due to the nat ure or extent of the defect, the Contractor shall submit written justification along wit h a proposed rectification schedule for approval of the Department. Any extension s hall be subject to the written approval of the competent authority. 5.5 Failure to attend to complaints or complete rectification within the stipulated timelines, without valid justification and approval, shall constitute a breach of contra ctual obligations and may invite appropriate contractual action, including recovery o f costs incurred by the Department for getting the work rectified through an alternat ive agency, at the Contractor's risk and cost, subject to the terms of the contract. 6. Periodic Inspection and Maintenance Reporting. 6.1 During the AMC period, the Contractor shall undertake preventive maintenan ce and inspection of the entire Battle Obstacle Course at least once every quarter (o nce in three months), or at such shorter intervals as may be prescribed by the Depa rtment. 6.2 Each inspection shall include verification of structural stability, integrity of joi nts and welds, condition of ropes, wooden components, fasteners, painting, anti-corr osion protection, barbed wire, pickets and all other components forming part of the obstacles. 6.3 The Contractor shall submit a written inspection and maintenance report afte r every scheduled visit, clearly indicating the condition of each obstacle, defects noti ced, repairs undertaken, replacements carried out and any safety-related observatio ns. 6.4 The Department shall be entitled to carry out independent inspections at any time and direct the Contractor to undertake necessary corrective maintenance withi n the stipulated timelines. 7. AMC Payment and Performance Monitoring. 7.1 The cost of the two-year AMC shall be clearly indicated as a separate compo nent in the financial bid, notwithstanding its inclusion in the overall quoted contract price. 7.2 AMC payments shall be released on a half-yearly basis, in arrears, subject to satisfactory performance of maintenance obligations during the relevant period and certification by the competent authority. 7.3 Release of AMC payments shall be subject to: 7.3.1. Completion of scheduled quarterly inspections. 7.3.2. Submission of prescribed inspection and maintenance reports. 7.3.3. Satisfactory rectification of reported defects and complaints. 7.3.4. Maintenance of all obstacles in safe, serviceable and operational cond ition. 7.3.5. Certification of satisfactory performance by the Department's nominat ed representative or competent authority. 7.4 The Department reserves the right to withhold the corresponding AMC paym ent, either wholly or partly, in respect of unsatisfactory or incomplete maintenance obligations, until the deficiencies have been rectified to its satisfaction, in accordanc

e with the applicable contractual provisions. 7.5 No AMC payment shall be admissible for any period during which the Contrac tor has failed to discharge the prescribed maintenance obligations, subject to the ter ms of the contract. 8. General Conditions and Contractor's Responsibility. 8.1 All repairs, maintenance and replacement activities shall be carried out using materials of equivalent or superior quality conforming to the original technical specifications and shall be subje ct to inspection and approval by the Department. 4 8.2 The Contractor shall ensure that all maintenance activities are undertaken without compro mising the structural integrity, safety standards, intended functionality or training utility of any obs tacle. 8.3 The Contractor shall remain responsible for defects, failures or damage attributable to sub standard materials, deficient workmanship, faulty fabrication, improper installation or inadequate maintenance, notwithstanding any inspection or acceptance of the work by the Department. 8.4 The Contractor shall not dismantle, modify, substitute or alter any structural component or design feature of an obstacle without prior written approval of the Department. 8.5 The Contractor shall not levy any additional charges for activities, materials, repairs or repl acements expressly covered under the warranty and AMC provisions of this contract. 8.6 The warranty and AMC obligations shall be binding on the Contractor and shall form an integra l and enforceable part of the contract. Failure to discharge these obligations shall be dealt with in a ccordance with the relevant provisions of the tender and contract agreement. Note:- Old Appx ‘C’ of Technical Specification may pl be treated as cancelled. Warranty and Annual Maintenance Contract (AMC) will be considered as per fresh Appx ‘C’ mentioned above. . 8.
